newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Israelis plead guilty on Cyprus escape charge.
newsitem.headline: Israelis plead guilty on Cyprus escape charge.

text.p: Three Israelis in Cyprus pleaded guilty on Wednesday to charges connected with their brief escape from custody last month when two of them held up a police car in central Nicosia last month to free two others in the car.

The criminal court, which convened in capital Nicosia, ordered that accused Shuki Samana 24, David Biton, 24, and Amon Shimon, 28, reappear before it on Monday. They will remain in custody until then, the court ordered.
A fourth defendant, David Biton's brother and telephone salesman Avi, 21, was jailed for two and a half years last week for the escape and for possession of forged dollar bills.
Shimon and David Biton face charges of helping Samana and Avi Biton escape as they were being taken from jail to a courthouse to stand trial on charges of possessing 72 forged $100 notes.

Brandishing a pistol -- which police now suspect was a toy gun -- David Biton and Shimon got the other two suspects out of the police vehicle, put them on the back of their motorcycles and charged through a United Nations checkpoint into Turkish-held northern Cyprus.
Turkish Cypriot police returned them the same day.
